patterns.title: Phased Execution and Step Signaling
patterns.short_description: Enforces strict sequential execution order among concurrently running threads using condition variables, semaphores, or countdown latches.
mental_triggers: Print in order: first() then second() then third() called concurrently by different threads
Coordinate execution phases where thread B must wait until thread A signals completion
Prevent race conditions on order of execution without busy-waiting polling
constraint_signals: Thread scheduling is non-deterministic; threads must block and wake up only when signaled by their predecessor

patterns.title: Critical Section Protection and Mutual Exclusion
patterns.short_description: Protects shared mutable state by ensuring only one thread executes a critical section at any given time using locks/mutexes.
mental_triggers: Prevent lost updates when multiple threads increment a shared counter
Synchronize read-modify-write cycles on shared data structures
Guard shared resource access with RAII lock guards or synchronized blocks
constraint_signals: Simultaneous writes to shared memory without synchronization cause undefined data races

patterns.title: Producer-Consumer & Bounded Queue Coordination
patterns.short_description: Coordinates producer threads generating work items and consumer threads processing them via a synchronized queue with wait/notify.
mental_triggers: Design Bounded Blocking Queue with fixed capacity
Manage worker thread pool processing tasks from an incoming task queue
Handle decoupled production and consumption rates with backpressure and no starvation
constraint_signals: Producer must wait when queue is full; consumer must wait when queue is empty

patterns.title: Cyclic Barriers and Thread Rendezvous
patterns.short_description: Synchronizes a fixed set of threads at a rendezvous barrier, holding each thread until all participants have arrived before proceeding.
mental_triggers: Building H2O: 2 hydrogen threads and 1 oxygen thread must assemble together before creating a molecule
Phased parallel computations where step T+1 requires all threads to complete step T
Reusable barrier for cyclic multi-round execution
constraint_signals: Threads arrive at different times but must release in exact stoichiometric or group ratios

patterns.title: Resource Pools and Permit Accounting
patterns.short_description: Controls access to a limited pool of identical resources using counting semaphores or token bucket permit management.
mental_triggers: Allow at most K concurrent connections to a resource pool
Rate-limit API requests to a fixed number of permits per time window
Acquire multiple permits atomically from a shared permit pool
constraint_signals: Resource pool size is fixed (K); threads requiring resources block until permits are released back to the pool

patterns.title: Phased Turn-Taking & Thread State Interleaving
patterns.short_description: Alternating execution turns across multiple threads according to cyclical or state-dependent turns without race conditions.
mental_triggers: Print FooBar Alternately: thread A prints Foo, thread B prints Bar in exact alternation
Print Zero Even Odd: thread 0 outputs 0, alternating with thread Even and thread Odd
Fizz Buzz Multithreaded: 4 threads coordinating on modulo 3, 5, 15, and number output
constraint_signals: Strict turn scheduling requires shared atomic state counters and condition variable broadcasts

patterns.title: Deadlock Avoidance & Resource Hierarchy
patterns.short_description: Preventing circular wait deadlocks across concurrent threads by enforcing strict lock ordering or limiting simultaneous holders.
mental_triggers: The Dining Philosophers: acquiring left and right forks in strict ascending address/id order
Traffic Light Controlled Intersection: controlling green light signals without vehicle gridlock
Preventing circular wait by ensuring resource acquisition order is global and strictly monotonic
constraint_signals: Multiple threads compete for overlapping pairs of resources; uncoordinated acquisition causes circular wait
patterns.base_template_py:
import threading

class AccountTransfer:
    def transfer(self, lock1: threading.Lock, lock2: threading.Lock, action) -> None:
        # Acquire locks in deterministic order of their object id to prevent cyclic deadlock
        first, second = (lock1, lock2) if id(lock1) < id(lock2) else (lock2, lock1)
        with first:
            with second:
                action()

hints.title: Asymmetric Grouping Constraint
hints.text: Independent threads arrive at random intervals and must be grouped into fixed ratio clusters before proceeding. How can multiple threads hold until an exact quota of complementary threads arrives?

hints.title: Permit Accounting and Barrier Rendezvous
hints.text: Permit counters restrict entry to two hydrogen threads and one oxygen thread at a time, while a synchronization barrier forces all three to arrive before any thread releases its element.

hints.title: Semaphore Throttling with Cyclic Barrier
hints.text: Initialize a hydrogen semaphore with 2 permits, an oxygen semaphore with 1 permit, and a cyclic barrier of size 3. When a hydrogen thread arrives, it acquires a permit, waits at the barrier, releases hydrogen, and restores its permit. Oxygen threads follow the same pattern with their semaphore.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from threading import Semaphore, Barrier

class H2O:
    def __init__(self):
        self.sem_h = Semaphore(2)
        self.sem_o = Semaphore(1)
        self.barrier = Barrier(3)

    def hydrogen(self, releaseHydrogen: 'Callable[[], None]') -> None:
        self.sem_h.acquire()
        self.barrier.wait()
        releaseHydrogen()
        self.sem_h.release()

    def oxygen(self, releaseOxygen: 'Callable[[], None]') -> None:
        self.sem_o.acquire()
        self.barrier.wait()
        releaseOxygen()
        self.sem_o.release()
```

complexity.notes: Group synchronization with 2:1 stoichiometric molecular barrier.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Without atomic grouping barriers, oxygen threads can outpace hydrogen or three hydrogens can bind simultaneously, violating the strict 2:1 stoichiometric molecular invariant. Spin-locking on thread counters risks deadlocks under thread starvation.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Two counting semaphores (2 permits for H, 1 permit for O) coupled with a 3-party barrier require O(1) auxiliary synchronization memory and guarantee exact (2H, 1O) molecular groups without unbounded thread queuing.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Ensuring exactly two hydrogen atoms pair with one oxygen before any party departs the barrier; releasing permits in finally blocks; preventing thread deadlocks when molecules arrive out of order.

hints.title: Capacity-Bounded Buffer Synchronization
hints.text: A fixed-capacity buffer must block producer threads when internal storage is full and block consumer threads when storage is empty. How do condition monitors coordinate capacity states?

hints.title: Dual Condition Formulation
hints.text: Guard the internal buffer with a mutual exclusion lock. Use condition variables to notify awaiting consumers when an element arrives and notify awaiting producers when a slot frees up.

hints.title: While Loop Invariant Check
hints.text: Always check queue fullness and emptiness inside while loops before proceeding to defend against spurious wakeups. Signal the counterpart condition after modifying queue state.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import threading
from collections import deque

class BoundedBlockingQueue:
    def __init__(self, capacity: int):
        self.capacity = capacity
        self.queue = deque()
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
        self.not_full = threading.Condition(self.lock)
        self.not_empty = threading.Condition(self.lock)

    def enqueue(self, element: int) -> None:
        with self.not_full:
            while len(self.queue) >= self.capacity:
                self.not_full.wait()
            self.queue.append(element)
            self.not_empty.notify()

    def dequeue(self) -> int:
        with self.not_empty:
            while len(self.queue) == 0:
                self.not_empty.wait()
            val = self.queue.popleft()
            self.not_full.notify()
            return val

    def size(self) -> int:
        with self.lock:
            return len(self.queue)
```

variables: C: capacity limit of the bounded queue
complexity.notes: Enqueue and dequeue operations perform amortized O(1) buffer mutations under condition synchronization.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Unsynchronized collections result in lost updates, race conditions on length calculations, and deadlocks.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Memory bounded strictly by capacity C prevents unbounded heap exhaustion under rapid producers.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use of while loop guards around wait() calls to guard against spurious wakeups.

solutions.approach: Monitor pattern with dual condition variables
ReentrantLock with notFull and notEmpty conditions

hints.title: Four-Way Divisibility Arbitration
hints.text: Four specialized threads must output words or numbers based on divisibility by 3 and 5 up to N. How can an integer state counter safely coordinate which thread is eligible to act?

hints.title: Barrier or Condition Monitor
hints.text: Protect the current counter value with a lock and condition variable. Each thread awakens when the counter satisfies its exact divisibility condition or when the counter exceeds N.

hints.title: Condition Notification Loop
hints.text: While the current counter is at most N, wait until divisibility matches. Perform the print invocation, increment the counter, and broadcast notification to all waiting threads.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Each number from 1 to N triggers exactly one print action with coordinated condition broadcast.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Four threads polling without condition synchronization create massive CPU spinning and non-deterministic interleaving.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: A single lock and condition monitor uses constant O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Correct loop exit conditions handling thread termination when counter exceeds N.

solutions.approach: Condition monitor with state-based notification broadcast

hints.title: Alternating Execution Coordination
hints.text: Two threads each run a loop, and their outputs must alternate exactly. What must each thread wait for before it prints, and what must it signal after printing?

hints.title: Paired Counting Permits
hints.text: Two binary synchronization semaphores can alternate permits between the two threads, ensuring each thread only advances when the other has finished its current turn.

hints.title: Dual Semaphore Ping-Pong
hints.text: Initialize a first semaphore with 1 permit and a second semaphore with 0 permits. In the foo loop, acquire the first semaphore, execute printFoo, and release the second semaphore. In the bar loop, acquire the second semaphore, execute printBar, and release the first semaphore.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Unsynchronized alternating loops produce race conditions where bar prints before foo or multiple foo calls interleave consecutively. Busy-waiting using volatile flags wastes CPU cycles and fails on weakly-ordered memory architectures.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Pairing two semaphores (or condition variables with a boolean predicate) requires O(1) memory and suspends threads during opposite turns, ensuring exact alternating lockstep in O(N) total operations.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Initializing the first semaphore with 1 permit and the second with 0; proper semaphore permit handoff (foo releases bar, bar releases foo); deadlock prevention and clean thread termination after N cycles.

hints.title: Phase Coordination Obstacle
hints.text: Three concurrent routines execute independently with unpredictable scheduling. How can earlier steps notify subsequent steps that prerequisite work has completed without busy waiting?

hints.title: Signaling Events and Latches
hints.text: Synchronization events allow threads to pause execution until a completion signal is received, enforcing strict sequential ordering between independent routines.

hints.title: Two-Event Chained Progression
hints.text: Initialize two event objects representing completion of the first and second steps. In the first method, run printFirst and set the first event. In the second method, wait on the first event before running printSecond and setting the second event. In the third method, wait on the second event before printing.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from threading import Event

class Foo:
    def __init__(self):
        self.first_done = Event()
        self.second_done = Event()

    def first(self, printFirst: 'Callable[[], None]') -> None:
        printFirst()
        self.first_done.set()

    def second(self, printSecond: 'Callable[[], None]') -> None:
        self.first_done.wait()
        printSecond()
        self.second_done.set()

    def third(self, printThird: 'Callable[[], None]') -> None:
        self.second_done.wait()
        printThird()
```

complexity.notes: Event-driven thread coordination with zero CPU busy-waiting.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Busy-waiting with while (!done); spins the CPU at 100% core utilization, creating thread contention, cache thrashing, and potential starvation under preemption or non-realtime OS thread schedulers.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Using two binary synchronization events/semaphores requires O(1) memory and suspends waiting threads without CPU consumption, ensuring sequential execution with zero thread drift.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Avoiding spinlocks / busy-waits; handling InterruptedException in Java / condition variable predicate spurious wakeups in C++; understanding why two coordination barriers are necessary to enforce a three-step sequence.

solutions.approach: Mutex and Condition Variable Sequence Synchronization

hints.title: Alternating Print Coordination
hints.text: Three concurrent threads must emit a strictly ordered sequence: zero followed alternately by odd and even integers up to N. How can signaling primitives coordinate the exact order of execution?

hints.title: Signaling Triad Formulation
hints.text: Configure three synchronization signals: one initialized to grant immediate execution to the zero emitter, and two initialized in waiting states for odd and even emitters.

hints.title: State Transition Logic
hints.text: After emitting zero for step i, unblock the odd emitter if i is odd, or the even emitter if i is even. Once the non-zero integer is printed, return control back to the zero emitter for the next cycle.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Executes 2N total thread context switches and emits each integer in strict alternating sequence.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Unsynchronized loops or spinning on atomic variables wastes CPU cycles through busy waiting and causes race conditions.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Constant space for three synchronization primitives provides deterministic ordering without auxiliary buffers.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Clean hand-off signaling between zero and alternating number threads with proper loop bounds for odd and even terminations.

hints.title: Resource Hierarchy or Capacity Restriction
hints.text: Five philosophers seated around a circular table share adjacent forks. If all five pick up their left fork simultaneously, a circular deadlock occurs. What resource constraint prevents deadlocks?

hints.title: Limiting Concurrency to 4 Eaters
hints.text: Allowing at most four philosophers to attempt eating at any moment guarantees by the pigeonhole principle that at least one philosopher can claim both forks and finish eating.

hints.title: Semaphore Guard and Fork Locks
hints.text: Acquire an eater semaphore initialized to 4. Then acquire both adjacent fork locks, perform eating actions, release the fork locks, and release the eater semaphore.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import threading

class DiningPhilosophers:
    def __init__(self):
        self.forks = [threading.Lock() for _ in range(5)]
        self.limit = threading.Semaphore(4)

    def wantsToEat(self,
                   philosopher: int,
                   pickLeftFork: 'Callable[[], None]',
                   pickRightFork: 'Callable[[], None]',
                   eat: 'Callable[[], None]',
                   putLeftFork: 'Callable[[], None]',
                   putRightFork: 'Callable[[], None]') -> None:
        left = philosopher
        right = (philosopher + 1) % 5

        with self.limit:
            with self.forks[left]:
                with self.forks[right]:
                    pickLeftFork()
                    pickRightFork()
                    eat()
                    putLeftFork()
                    putRightFork()
```

complexity.notes: Each meal involves acquiring bounded synchronization locks in constant time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Symmetric lock acquisition without limiting eaters creates a circular wait condition leading to deadlock.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Constant auxiliary storage for 5 fork locks and 1 counting semaphore.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Formal explanation of how the 4-eater limit or asymmetric fork ordering breaks Coffman deadlock conditions.

hints.title: Single Direction Road Mutual Exclusion
hints.text: Cars arrive randomly at an intersection connecting Road 1 and Road 2. Cars traveling on the current green road may proceed immediately. What synchronization primitive protects light switching?

hints.title: Active Green Road State Guard
hints.text: Maintain an integer variable recording the currently active green road. Protect light checks and signal changes with a mutual exclusion lock.

hints.title: Conditional Signal Switch and Car Passage
hints.text: When a car arrives from roadId, acquire the lock. If roadId differs from current green road, invoke changeGreen() and update the state variable. Then invoke crossCar() and release the lock.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import threading

class TrafficLight:
    def __init__(self):
        self.green_road = 1
        self.lock = threading.Lock()

    def carArrived(
        self,
        carId: int,
        roadId: int,
        direction: int,
        changeGreen: 'Callable[[], None]',
        crossCar: 'Callable[[], None]'
    ) -> None:
        with self.lock:
            if self.green_road != roadId:
                self.green_road = roadId
                changeGreen()
            crossCar()
```

complexity.notes: Each car arrival processes light state checking and crossing within a constant time critical section.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Unsynchronized direction changes cause multiple cars from intersecting roads to enter simultaneously.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Requires only a single lock and integer state variable.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Simple serializing lock ensuring thread-safe road direction transitions.
